draft.title: Oxidation numbers
card: An oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if all its bonding electrons went to the more electronegative atom. It is a bookkeeping tool that tracks electrons.
An atom in an element is 0. A simple ion has its own charge. Oxygen is usually -2 and hydrogen is usually +1. The numbers in a neutral compound add to 0, and in an ion they add to its charge.
Use known numbers to find the unknown one. In SO2, oxygen is -2 twice, which is -4, so sulfur must be +4.
If an atom's oxidation number rises in a reaction, it is oxidised. If it falls, it is reduced.
draft.remember: Work out each oxidation number from the rules. A rise means oxidised and a fall means reduced.

a.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion, MnO4⁻?
a.why: Four oxygen atoms at -2 give -8. The total must equal the ion's charge of -1, so Mn is +7. The answer -1 is the charge of the whole ion, not of manganese alone.
a.clue: The numbers must add up to the charge on the ion.

b.q: Zinc reacts with copper(II) sulfate: Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu. Which statement is correct?
opts: Zn goes from 0 to +2 and is oxidised
Zn goes from 0 to +2 and is reduced
Cu goes from +2 to 0 and is oxidised
Cu goes from 0 to +2 and is reduced
b.why: Zinc's number rises from 0 to +2, so zinc is oxidised. Copper falls from +2 to 0, so it is reduced. The second option has the right numbers but the wrong label, because a rise is oxidation.
b.clue: Find each metal's number before and after, then see whether it rose or fell.

b.best: Zn goes from 0 to +2 and is oxidised

problems.detail: The why refers to 'the second option', but options are shown in random order, so the reference may point to the wrong option. Two options also have the right numbers but the wrong label ('Cu goes from +2 to 0 and is oxidised' and 'Zn goes from 0 to +2 and is reduced'), so the reference is ambiguous anyway. Name the option by its text instead.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct (Mn is +7; Zn is oxidised from 0 to +2). The only problem is that why (b) refers to 'the second option' by position, which breaks when options are shuffled and is ambiguous because two options have the right numbers but the wrong label.
